preOptimization.note: Reported by team-lead based on prior CI runs after Welle-D bump (12-yaml ruleset / 342 rules / 91 custom-fns). Stripe-full spec is 7.95 MB / 1385 schemas / 414 paths.

preOptimizationProfile_walkers_modules_o.spectralColdMs: not-measured (was running > 30min in standalone profile-script before bash-background-task killed it; behaviour matches the 23.7-min reported test-runtime)

comparativeProfile_dnd5eapi.note: dnd5eapi is small (49 schemas, 47 paths). The single-pass cycle/null-strip alone explains the ~50% spectral-cold reduction by halving the deep-clone cost on the spec tree before passing to spectral.run(). Module Promise.all is responsible for the runModules-combined improvement.

comparativeProfile_pagerdutyFull.note: pagerduty-full (272 schemas, 246 paths, 2.5MB) — spectral runtime 2:58 min, walker+module ~13s post-parallelization. Single-pass strip helps but the rule-engine itself dominates.

optimizationsApplied.name: single-pass cycle-strip + null-strip
optimizationsApplied.rationale: Previous implementation was two full deep-clones of the spec tree (cycleStripSpec then stripNulls). Now combined into one traversal via cycleStripAndNullStrip(). On stripe-full's 8MB tree this halves the pre-Spectral preprocessing-cost.

optimizationsApplied.name: runModules() Promise.all parallelization
optimizationsApplied.rationale: ajv-validator (~15s) and codegen-validation (~12s) are by far the slowest modules and run serially before. They are I/O-bound on their own internal compilation work, not on the JS event-loop, so concurrent execution converges to max(individual) wallclock rather than sum.

optimizationsApplied.name: runWalkers() Promise.all parallelization
optimizationsApplied.rationale: Walker total serial ~3.2s on stripe-full; max single walker ~1.4s. Promise.all converges to max wallclock.

optimizationsApplied.name: schema-similarity bucketing
optimizationsApplied.rationale: Mathematical bound: max-Jaccard between schemas of property-counts m and M (m ≤ M) is m / M. So if M > m / 0.8 = 1.25m we can prove sim < 0.8 without computing it. We bucket fingerprints by exact property-count and only iterate candidate buckets. On stripe-full (1385 schemas) this drops the worst-case ~960k pairwise comparisons to typically ~50-100k. Behaviour preserved (same pairs detected).
optimizationsApplied.measuredImpactStripe: schema-similarity walker 437ms → expected ~50-200ms (Stripe full retest didn't profile this individually post-opt)

optimizationsApplied.name: recursiveSchemaNeedsMaxDepth refactor: O(N · graph-walk) → O(V + E)
optimizationsApplied.rationale: Pre-refactor: each of N schemas walked the entire raw object tree to detect direct or transitive references to itself. Post-refactor: single pre-pass extracts every schema's direct $ref targets into Map<name, Set<targetName>>, then per-schema reachability check walks only the tiny adjacency graph. Behaviour preserved (verified by 83/83 threat-p2-rules tests passing).

postOptimization.githubRestNewTimeoutSetting: 2700000ms (45min) — previously 900000ms (15min); github-rest is 12.5MB vs stripe-full 8MB and was already failing post-Welle-D before any changes here.

remainingBottleneck: Spectral.run() itself accounts for >95% of total runtime on stripe-full (22+ min of the 22.85min total). The cost is intrinsic to the engine: 342 rules including 109 with `$..` recursive-descent JSONPath filters, run by Nimma against an 8 MB document tree. Walker+module-layer Promise.all parallelization saves ~13s wallclock (mostly from ajv ↔ codegen overlap). Further reduction would require:
remainingBottleneckOptions: Narrowing the 109 `$..` rules to specific subtrees (e.g. `$.paths[*][*].responses[*].content..schema..` instead of `$..` where possible). This is rule-level surgery, scope = Welle-D follow-up.
Forking Spectral / building a custom rule-engine. Out of scope.

Splitting the test file: run dnd5eapi / stripe-full / pagerduty-full / github-rest in separate test files so vitest can parallelize them across workers (default vitest config). Wallclock would converge to max(individual) instead of sum.
oq4Recommendations: Function-consolidation candidates spotted in profile (no direct duplicates in the slowest set, but several candidate clusters):

1. `*-needs-rate-limit-headers` family (sensitive-flow, login, signup, posting-comment) all share the same shape: `op-classification → declared-rate-limit-header check`. Extract a single `requiresRateLimitHeaders(opClassification)` helper and have each rule pass its predicate.

2. `*-content-type-correct` and `*-rejects-wildcard-content-type` and `multipart-form-bundle` and `merge-patch-properties-not-required` and `json-patch-schema-is-array` all share `requestBody.content[<exact-mt>]`-shape inspection. Helper: `forEachRequestBodyMediaType(op, predicate)`.

3. `*-needs-security` family (object-id-write-op, admin-description, non-standard-method, signup-needs-rate-limit-or-captcha) all walk the operation+spec security stack. Helper: `effectiveSecurityFor(op, doc)`.
4. The threat-p2 + threat-p3 file split is along Welle boundary, not along function-shape. OQ-4 may consider grouping by predicate-family across yaml-files.
